sections.what_happened: Vucic conceded defeat in Serbia's Oct 25 snap parliamentary election: 'It is clear that we have lost these elections' / 'The Students' List has won.' CeSID-Ipsos projection (56% of processed sample): Students' List 52% / 135-140 of 250 seats vs SNS-led alliance 39.3% / ~104-105 seats; minority parties ~7 seats. Vucic's own figures: Students' List 2.2m votes vs SNS 1.7m. Turnout ~67-68% by 19:00 local, highest since 1992. Belgrade street celebrations; crowds dismantled the pro-Vucic loyalist camp in central Belgrade. Vucic blamed independent media, unnamed European countries and an 'American deep state', said he will not flee and will not appeal the result in court. CRTA watchdog reported pressure on voters/workers at almost a third of 500 monitored stations and ballot-secrecy failures; CeSID logged ~260 irregularity reports by 17:00 GMT. Official final results still pending/counting continuing at last check.
sections.what_verified: Concession confirmed by the loser himself on live TV; seat split is a CeSID/Ipsos projection, NOT an official final count
sections.what_disputed: Seat numbers are projections from a sample, not the State Election Commission final count (official results limited, counting continuing, one Leskovac station extended to 23:00 local after a violent confrontation); Vucic's 'foreign interference' blame is an ALLEGATION, unproven; turnout figures differ between the commission, monitors and the students (67.6-69.1%). CNN also carried the concession but has NO declared tier in the registry and is NOT counted; CeSID/Ipsos as pollster has NO declared tier and is NOT counted toward corroboration.
sections.why_matters: The students who started with a collapsed canopy just ended 14 years of Vucic -- and the loser conceded on live TV while blaming a foreign plot. Counted projection vs official count: what is confirmed, what is still a projection.
sections.context: Background: CATCH-UP ELEVATION -- Serbia: Vucic concedes, student-led list wins outright majority, ending 14 years of SNS rule
